body:
The maintainer said in chat on 2026-11-22: "PR's with merge-ready cannot have needs-rework at the same time.."

## The rule today
`AGENTS.md`, "Only collaborators' reviews count": a PR whose current head has a collaborator's change request and also `merge-ready` (or `merge-ready` with `needs-rework`) is a disagreement. `/merge-ready` reports it. "No agent removes a label. The two collaborators decide on the PR."

## The new rule
1. `merge-ready` and `needs-rework` are never on the same PR.
2. The person or agent that sets one of the two labels removes the other label in the same step, with one comment that says why.
3. A disagreement between two collaborators on the same head: `needs-rework` stays and `merge-ready` is removed. An open change request wins. The collaborator who set `merge-ready` gets the comment.
4. This replaces the text "No agent removes a label" for these two labels.

## Files to change
- `AGENTS.md`: the rule "Only collaborators' reviews count" (the disagreement items) and the "Review labels" table.
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`
- `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md` and the `PR-reviewer` agent file, where they set a review label.
- `.claude/skills/resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md`
- Each other skill or agent file that cites the old disagreement text (search for `needs-rework` and `disagreement`).

## Done means
- The files above state the new rule with the same words in each place.
- No file keeps the old text for these two labels.
- The PR body has the line `Process change: yes`. The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.
- If an `xtask` test pins the old text, the test changes with it.

body:
### What happens

On two Windows 11 machines (bacon: Intel NUC with iGPU; lenny: desktop), the Windows quick check of `main` is red on one step:

```
FAIL  ui suites: lib  exit 101
process didn't exit successfully: `...\camcraft_ui-b30d80154151484e.exe --test-threads=12` (exit code: 0xc0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION)
```

The binary dies after about 100 tests with a native access violation, not a failed assert. Last tests printed before the crash (bacon, main `7a626a7f5`): the `egui_app::setup_plane_tests` / `setup_points_tests` group.

### It is a concurrency crash

The same binary, same tree, run single-threaded on bacon:

```
camcraft_ui-b30d80154151484e.exe --test-threads=1
test result: ok. 1425 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored; finished in 166.04s
```

Linux (len, post-merge runners) and macOS (m3) are green on the same commits. Likely candidates: tests that create a graphics device/adapter (wgpu) or another thread-unsafe native resource in parallel. Related but different: #3258 (several UI binaries on one Linux host, fixed by #3302 naming the crash status); this one is one binary, several test threads, on Windows.

### Workaround

`--test-threads=1` for `camcraft-ui --lib` on Windows (the gate stays slower but green).

**Done means:** `cargo xtask gate quick` on Windows runs `ui suites: lib` green at its normal thread count, or the gate serialises exactly the tests that share the native resource, with a test or gate-plan pin and the crashing resource named in the decision note.

**Triage.** P3: a red gate on Windows only, with a workaround; no wrong output. `effort:medium`: test harness / gate plan, one crate.

Depends on #3371

A form bit cuts an edge, not a wall. This is a new law, not an offset by a radius (the #3351 body says the same). It is slice 1, step 3 and step 4 of the research in #896, for a non-undercut `FormMill`.

1. Edge form law in 2D Chamfer: the user gives the edge loop and the form depth. The cutter axis rides at the offset `rho(z_low)` from the wall, where `z_low` is the lowest height of the form band. The tip height puts the top of the form band on the top face. For a roundover of radius `R` and pilot radius `r_p`: offset `r_p`, and the arc meets the wall and the top face tangentially.
2. The pilot band clears the wall by the gouge tolerance. The pilot never touches the part.
3. `EdgeBreak` (`crates/cl/src/cl/edge_break.rs`) and `credit_breaks` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/edge_break.rs`) credit a circular break and a general form break (the meridian swept along the edge), beside the planar bevel of today.
4. Where the model already has the rounded edge, the cut must match it with no credit.
5. Trace and Engrave admit a `FormMill` with a non-decreasing meridian (a groove or bead along a line).
6. Open the 2D Chamfer door that #3369 closed, for a non-undercut `FormMill`.

## Rules

- `effort:max`: a new toolpath law (safety floor).
- The `Taper` chamfer toolpaths and goldens do not change (pinned).

## Done means

- A roundover bit rounds the top edge of a brick in 2D Chamfer, verifies clean, passes `posting::verification_gate` and posts (pinned, with a golden). This is the "Done means" of #896 for corner rounding.

Add one internal shape type in `camcraft-tools`: the tool meridian. It is the cutting outline `rho(z)`, tip up, made of lines and circular arcs. All consumers read the tool shape through it in later sub-issues.

1. A new module (for example `crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`, under 400 lines). It holds the meridian type and `Tool::meridian()`. Reuse the point form of `SpunProfile` (`crates/tools/src/spun.rs`: `z`, `r`, signed `arc`).

It agrees with `Tool::profile` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:387-465`) on the cutting band.
3. A split of the meridian into convex atoms:
   - a straight segment gives a frustum (each slope);
   - an arc that bulges away from the axis gives a torus zone;
   - an arc that bulges toward the axis gives chord frusta (outer bound) or tangent frusta (inner bound), with a sag limit as a parameter.
4. Each atom carries a flag: cutting, or non-cutting (a pilot bearing band).

- The geometry is from elementary plane geometry (chord sag `R (1 - cos(theta / 2))`) and convexity (Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, 3.2.5). Each module has its provenance line. No HSMWorks material.

The option "write the stock as a Manual Guide i blank" in `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` writes `G1902` or `G1900` before the first section. The guard at about line 602 refuses a WCS that is rotated about Z, and writes the comment `(NO BLANK BLOCK - <reason>)`.

The guard does not check a tilted (indexed) first setup. If the first section has a tilted work plane, the blank block can use the world axes. The simulation on the control can then show the blank in the wrong orientation. No comment tells the user.

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> issue; enhancement; support for tapered tooling like ball mills, roundover bits and similar, router style tooling.

## What exists now

- `ToolKind::Taper` is a cone with a sharp virtual tip (a chamfer mill). It has no tip diameter and no tip radius (#895, P8). The 2D Chamfer reads it.
- The spun cutter outline is display only. No generator, no simulation and no gouge law reads it (#896, P8). So a roundover bit, a dovetail or a lollipop cannot be used in an operation.
- Lollipop cutters are in #1974, #1893 and #1955 (P6 to P8). Router machines are in #1915, #3038 and #3192.

## Wanted

The user can define and use these tools, and the operations, the simulation and the gouge and collision laws all use the real shape:

1. Tapered end mill: a cone with a flat tip or a ball tip, and a taper half-angle. Examples: tapered ball nose for 3D carving, tapered flat end mill.
2. Roundover bit: a quarter-circle profile with a pilot or without one. It cuts an edge radius.
3. Other router-style form bits: chamfer bit, cove bit, ogee, dovetail, V-groove bit.
4. A generic form-cutter kind whose profile (a spun outline) is read by the generators, the simulation and the checks. The named bits above are profiles of it, with a library entry each.

## Plan (research first)

This issue is `needs-research`. The research answers these questions and files sub-issues. It writes no code.

- One shape model for all of them: a profile (radius and height pairs, lines and arcs) that the collision, gouge and stock-removal code reads. Compare this with the separate kinds that exist now (`Taper`, `BallNose`, `BullNose`). Decide how #895, #896 and #1974 fold in, or stay separate.
- Which operations take a form cutter: 3D finishing passes, 2D Contour with a profile bit (a roundover along an edge), Chamfer, Engrave. Which do not, and the named refusal for each.
- The offset law: the cutter centre path for a profile tool. A roundover bit follows an edge at the height where its arc touches. This is a new law, not an offset by a radius.
- The simulation: the cut volume of a swept profile on the CPU engine and on the GPU path (#2607).
- The tool library entries and the project-file change (a version bump).
- The post: no change in the G-code words. The tool data goes in the tool table.

## Rules

- Each sub-issue is P4, `enhancement`, `source:agent`, with its effort by the table. Work that changes the toolpath, the gouge check or the simulation is under the safety floor (`effort:high` or more).
- Specs and shapes come from public tool catalogues and machine-tool handbooks. Nothing from HSMWorks material.
- The tool kinds go through the same undoable commands and MCP tools as the existing tools.

## Done means

- The research is posted on this issue: the shape model, the table of operations, and the sub-issue list.
- This issue closes when the sub-issues are filed. The sub-issues are picked for code.

body:
Refs #1448. Part of #1448. Follow-up of #3324.

## Why

The design of #3324 (`docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-shared.md`, section 2) chooses an operation-level project key for the start and exit picks. The PR of #3324 does not move the storage. The move puts one field on every path variant of `OpParams` and its DTO. More than ten open PRs change `wire_edm.rs` and `wire_edm_dto.rs`, so the move in the same PR conflicts with all of them.

The accessor `OpParams::path_picks()` hides the storage, so the family slices of #1448 that have a `links` field do not wait for this issue.

## What to do

- Store `camcraft_motion::path_picks::PathPicks` on every path kind.
- Write the key `picks: { start: [[x, y, z?], ...], exit: [...] }` at the operation level. Write it only when a list is not empty.
- Read the old keys on load: `links.approach.start_point`, `links.approach.exit_point` and the wire `start`.
- Keep the digest bytes `0xC7` / `0xC8` for the same values. No contour golden changes.
- Move `Approach::start_point` / `exit_point` and `WireContourOp.start` into the new field. Change `start_exit_rows.rs`, `start_exit_pick.rs` and the contour planner to read `path_picks()`.

## Done means

- A load test opens a file with the old `links.approach.start_point` key and a file with the old wire `start` key. The picks are the same after the load.
- Every contour golden and every contour pick test stays green with no change.
- This merges before the first family slice of #1448 for a kind with no `links` field (Face, turning, plasma).

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> bug; boundaries; we should have control over how much the "outside boundary" offset is and the "inside boundary" offset is.. now its just boundary offset, which when i shrink it to a negative value also offsets the boundary from the face/edge i picked. Which makes it problematic to control the boundaries using the strategies choosen for example "Open-Machine side B". generates a very generous outside boundary that makes you cut air for a good halv a minute.

## What happens

The Boundary group has one row, "Boundary offset" (`AreaControls::offset`, `crates/app/src/operation/types/area.rs:86`; row in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/boundary.rs:114`). Its hint says: "+ grows the area outward, - shrinks it inward". The one value moves the whole area edge: the edge that the user picked (the face or the edge chain) and the outer boundary (the stock outline that an open boundary runs on to).

The user wants the outer boundary to be tighter. He sets a negative offset. The picked edge moves as well, so the area no longer starts at the face or edge that he picked. He cannot get both.

## The cost

With "Open - machine side B" the area is the part between the picked chain and the stock outline. The outer boundary is "very generous". The tool cuts air for about half a minute. The user has no way to shrink only that outer side.

## Expected

Two offsets, each with its own row and hint:

1. Offset of the picked edge or face (the inside boundary): moves the line that the user picked. Default 0.
2. Offset of the outer boundary (the outside boundary: the stock outline, or the open boundary's run-on): moves only that line. Default 0.

Each one applies to a closed boundary and an open boundary. A closed boundary that has only the picked loop uses the first one. The "Extend past open edges" value is separate, as it is now.

## Rules

- The default of both is 0 and the output is byte-identical for a project that has one `offset` value of 0. A project with a non-zero `offset` loads as the same value in BOTH new offsets: the output stays the same (project-file version bump and a migration test).
- The change is an undoable command (`EditOperationParams`). The MCP tool gets both fields.
- The region and the verify check read the same two values. The planner never refuses the picked line because the outer offset is negative.
- Safety floor: this changes the machined region. The pin goes red first, the review is an independent Opus read, and the heavy lanes that the diff reaches run.

## Done means

- A pin test: an open boundary, side B, on a model with a stock larger than the part. With the outer offset negative and the picked offset 0, the region edge on the picked chain stays on the chain, and the outer edge moves in. The cut-air length drops by the measured amount.
- A structural test of the two rows (labels, hints, default).
- The project-file migration test and a byte-identical golden for an old project.

## What the repository shows

The maintainer is right: the stock removal does not run on the GPU. The plan exists. It is built only in part.

- #2607 (research, closed) decided: "The GPU does the display playback cut. The CPU f64 engines keep each verdict. The home for GPU compute code is `camcraft-gpu` (#2620)." It made the slices S1 to S6.
- S1 #2626 (the CPU f32 twin of the cell cut kernel) is merged. It is a CPU twin, by design. It runs no shader.
- #2620 (the `camcraft-gpu` compute crate: probe, cached device, CPU fallback) is NOT merged. Its work is held on the pushed branch `issue/2620-gpu-compute-seam` at `90c98be93`, since 2026-11-19 (the gate stopped for disk space). Its label is `claimed`, P4.
- S2 #2627 (the WGSL removal kernel for ball and flat tools, linear moves), S3 #2629 (viewport playback on the GPU, with CPU fallback), S4 #2628, S5 #2630 and S6 #2631 are open at P4. S3 to S6 are `blocked`.
- So the playback in the viewport still uses the CPU engines. A long program is slow.

## What the maintainer needs

The Simulate view plays a program at a usable speed, with a visible stock cut. The frame target is under 10 ms for a still frame (`docs/decisions/2238-frame-cost-rule.md`).

## Plan

1. Measure first. A scout and a worker time the playback on a real program (the `fig8` 2D Offset, EM-0800-4FL, and one 3D Pocket). The numbers go in a comment: cells, moves, milliseconds for each frame and for the cut. This shows where the time goes: the cut, the mesh, the upload, or the frame.
2. Quick wins on the CPU path that the measure shows, if any. Each has a counter test (AGENTS.md "Frame cost").
3. Finish the GPU path in order: #2620, then #2627 (S2), then #2629 (S3). Raise their priority to P2 and the type to bug (they are the fix of this issue). S4, S5 and S6 stay P4 and follow.
4. The CPU f64 engines keep each verdict (the verify check, the collision check, the post gate). The GPU result is display only. A machine without a usable GPU falls back to the CPU path and says so.

## Safety

The simulation that blocks the post is not changed by this work. Any change to the f64 engines is under the safety floor.

## Done means

- A recorded measure before and after, in a comment.
- On the reference machine, the Simulate view of a `fig8` program plays at a usable frame rate.
- A counter test: a still frame cuts nothing again.
- A CPU fallback test for a machine without a GPU.

body:
Refs #1448. Part of #1448.

## Why

The maintainer set the scope of #1448 on 2026-11-22: a user-set start point and exit point on EVERY operation that cuts a path. He asked for one shared mechanism: one command, one MCP tool, one viewport pick, one pair of rows. He set it to `bug` and `P2`: "Mark them as P2 - they are bugs at this point".

Today only the closed 2D Contour rings take a start point and an exit point. The kind table is in the research comment on #1448. Each family sub-issue of #1448 depends on this issue.

The shared design is recorded in `docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-shared.md` before the next slice (comment on #1448, 2026-11-22).

## What `main` has

- `Approach::start_point` / `exit_point` (`crates/motion/src/approach.rs:162,168`): `Option<Point2>`, model XY in mm, inside `links.approach`.
- Kinds with a `links` field: Contour, Pocket, Adaptive2D, Offset2D, Circular, Slot, Pocket3D, RotaryOffset, MultiAxisRough, Bore. The other 33 path kinds have no `links`.
- The project keys `links.approach.start_point` / `exit_point` (`crates/app/src/project/approach.rs:77,81`). The digest bytes `0xC7` / `0xC8` (`crates/app/src/operation/params/digest.rs:202-212`).
- `EditOperationParams` (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/edit.rs`). `named_refusal` runs at create, edit and load (`sane.rs:54`).
- MCP: the generic patch of `edit_operation` (`crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:304-318`). The schema does not name the fields.
- UI: `start_exit_rows.rs` and `start_exit_pick.rs`, only on the 2D Contour lead tab (`approach_page.rs:140-182`).
- A second, separate start field: `WireContourOp.start` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/wire_edm.rs:61-63`).

## Open questions, options and the recommended option

### 1. One shared type

- A: Keep the fields in `links.approach`, and add `links` to each kind that has none.
- B: A new shared type in `camcraft-motion`, for example `PathPicks { start, exit }`. Every path kind holds it. One accessor `OpParams::path_picks()` reads it for every kind. The contour moves its two fields into it. Wire Contour moves `start` into it.
- C: A field for each kind.

Recommended: B. Option A gives `links` to kinds that have no links (turning, EDM, plasma), and the field has no meaning there. Option C repeats the refusal law 43 times.

Sub-question: the shape of a pick. Today it is a 2D point. A 3D finishing start, a multi-axis start and a turning (Z, X) start need more. Recommended: a pick holds a model-frame point with an optional Z. Each family projects it in its own frame (setup XY, the tilted frame, the lathe (Z, X) plane). Sub-question: one pick for each operation, or one for each chain or region (the #1448 body says "one pick per chain or region"). Recommended: the type holds a list from the first slice, so that the file format does not change again. A first slice can refuse a list longer than one by name.

### 2. The project key

- A: Keep `links.approach.start_point` / `exit_point`.
- B: A new key at the operation level (for example `picks: { start: [...], exit: [...] }`). The loader also reads the old `links.approach.*` keys and the old wire `start` key, so every saved file opens unchanged.

Recommended: B, with the old keys read on load. The digest keeps `0xC7` / `0xC8` for the same values, so a contour golden does not change.

### 3. The command

- A: `EditOperationParams`, as today.
- B: A dedicated `SetStartExit` command.

Recommended: A. One undo step can then change the pick and the "Pass starts at" option of #3316 together. The maintainer asked for one command.

### 4. The MCP tool

- A: The generic patch of `edit_operation`, as today, with the fields named in its schema.
- B: A dedicated tool, for example `set_start_exit`.

Recommended: A, with the fields named in the schema of `edit_operation` and a read-only answer (in the kind description) that says which kinds take a pick. Option B gives two doors to one command.

### 5. The viewport pick and the rows

- Recommended: one capability for each kind in `KindInfo` (`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`), for example `Ring`, `Region`, `HoleOrder`, `Ends`, `Raster`, `NotTaken(reason)`.
- The pick snaps by capability: a wall for `Ring`, a point inside the region for `Region`, a hole for `HoleOrder`, an end for `Ends`, a corner for `Raster`.
- The rows of `start_exit_rows.rs` move to a shared group. Every operation page draws it.
- A kind with `NotTaken` draws the row with the reason by name (the maintainer: "Where a kind has no free start, the Start point row says so by name").

### 6. How the path is generated again to the point

- The pick is an input of the planner. The command changes the parameters. The normal generate runs after it, as for the contour today.
- Recommended: promote the ring helpers of `contour_start.rs` (`nearest_on_ring`, `reach`, `lead_held`) to a shared module in `crates/motion/src/`, for every ring and chain family.
- Each family keeps its own seam: re-sequence a ring, place the descent in a region, order the holes, choose an end, choose a raster corner.

### 7. Beside "Pass starts at" of #3316

- #3316 adds one shared parameter "Pass starts at: Auto / Inside / Outside" and its decision file `docs/decisions/3316-pass-start-shared.md`. This issue does not change it.
- The two choices work together. The pass side chooses which ring of a level cuts first. The start point chooses the place on that ring, and the descent place.
- Recommended order: the planner applies the pass side first, then projects the start pick onto the first ring that the pass side gives.
- A pick that the pass side makes impossible is refused by name. Example: "Outside" with a start pick inside the part.
- The design file names `3316-pass-start-shared.md` and keeps the two parameters as two fields in the same parameter group.

### 8. The refusal when a point cannot be reached

- A: Refuse by name (the contour law today).
- B: Move the pick to the nearest legal point and add a warning.

Recommended: A. The maintainer: "a pick is a wish. The planner refuses it by name when the lead law or the safety laws cannot hold it. It never moves the pick without a note."

Where each refusal runs:
- At command creation (`named_refusal`): the kind does not take a pick, the pick is not finite, or the pick is outside the setup.
- At generation: no lead fits, the helix does not fit, the pick is too far from the path, the pick conflicts with the pass side. The operation is refused, and the post is blocked.

Each message names the operation kind, the pick (start or exit), the reason and the user's next step.

## Done means

- `docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-shared.md` records each answer above: the choice, the reason and the dropped options.
- The shared type, the project key with the read of the old keys, the `edit_operation` schema fields, the `KindInfo` capability and the shared row group are on `main`.
- Every contour golden and every contour pick test stays green with no change.
- A load test opens a file with the old `links.approach.start_point` key and a file with the old wire `start` key.
- No family planner change is in this issue. The family sub-issues of #1448 do that.

He sent a screenshot of the Simulate view. It is not attached here.

## What happens

The generated toolpath cuts into the part. The planner does not keep the tool at its offset from the edge boundary. This is not a setting that the user chose. It is the planner.

## What the screenshot shows

- A close view of the viewport in Simulate. The part is a raised island with a figure-8 outline. The tool stands next to the island.
- A broad orange band runs along the wall of the part, at the top edge, around the curved outline. The maintainer reads this band as the cut into the part. The worker confirms what the orange marks in this build.

The operation page shows the warning `move 522 cuts past the finish surface - repeated on 62 more moves (to 1710)`. That warning is the same defect: the moves 522 to 1710 go past the finish surface. It is a separate defect from the slotting of #3316 (the ring order) and from the three rapids of #3319. The ring order may put the tool near the wall, but the offset of the tool from the boundary is wrong whatever the order.

## Expected

For an "Outside" containment, the tool centre stays one tool radius (4.000 mm for the Ø8 tool) plus the boundary offset away from the part edge. The tool never goes past the finish surface. The generator never makes a path that its own verify check refuses.

If the fix changes the offset geometry or the ring order, it is under the safety floor: the pin goes red first, and the review is an independent Opus read with a hand trace of one move.

## Where to look

- The offset of the boundary by the tool radius for the Outside band, and the corner handling of the figure-8 outline (two concave arcs).
- The code of `crates/motion/src/machining2d/` for the 2D Offset kind.
- The test `shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` (the known-fail pin of #2849) uses the same model and tool. Its body says the last feed ends 31.406 mm from the outline where 4 mm is expected. The worker checks if it is the same defect.

Two separate switches. "Origin axes" hides the axes only. "Grid" hides the grid only.

- The issue #2818 (closed) added the "Grid" box. It was written so that the box "hides the grid alone". It did not make the axes switch independent of the grid.

## Fix

The grid depends on `show_grid` only. The axes depend on `show_world_axes` only. Update the two comments. Add a test: with the axes hidden and the grid on, the grid is drawn.

## Not changed

The saved view preferences keep both keys. A project that hid the axes before shows the grid again after the change. Say this in the changelog row.

> explpain these two errors.. travels.. should never be anywhere but at clearance plane.. so why does it do G0s below it?

and then: "file that as a P1 Bug."

## What happens

A 2D Offset operation generates rapid moves (G0) that run sideways below the clearance plane. They cross stock that is still uncut. The operation page shows this warning:

`rapid move 543 travels through stock (below the clearance plane, or at it below the stock top) - repeated on 2 more moves (to 1711)`

So three lateral rapids (move 543 up to move 1711) are below the clearance plane.

## Expected

"Hop below clearance" is off. The Heights tab says: "off, every link climbs to Clearance Z". Every lateral rapid then rides at the clearance plane (Z 32.000 here). No rapid runs sideways through stock.

## Evidence

- Build v0.25.0, commit 7e2a8119. The maintainer sent screenshots. They are not attached here.
- Operation `2D Offset1`: tool `EM-0800-4FL` (Ø8), model `fig8`, Setup1, VMC 3-AXIS, Siemens 840D. The Outside containment is the same as in #3316.
- Heights tab: Clearance Z = Top of stock +10 (Z 32.000). Top Z = Top of stock +0 (Z 22.000). Bottom Z = Selection +1.5 (Z 1.500). Stepdown 10 mm. "Hop below clearance" off.
- Lead in / Lead out tab: Level to level "Same as entry". Between levels "Clearance plane". Between passes "Retract plane". Plunge "Height above material" 2.0 mm. Entry Helix, radius 1.6 mm.
- Status: `OK - 1764 moves - 2 warnings`. The second warning is `move 522 cuts past the finish surface - repeated on 62 more moves (to 1710)`.

## What the code says (read by the coordinator on 2026-11-22)

- With the hop off, `retract_z` is `None`. Then `levels.rs:179` sets `hop_z = retract_z.unwrap_or(clearance_z).min(clearance_z)`. A link with the choice "Retract plane" lifts to the clearance plane (Z 32). There is no hidden retract plane (see #3318).
- So the three lateral rapids below Z 32 do not come from a pass link. Their source is not known. The worker finds it.

## Safety

The verifier flags these rapids and the post is blocked, so no wrong program is posted today. A rapid through stock is the failure that the verifier exists to stop. The generator must not make one. The priority is P1 on the word of the maintainer.

## Possible links

- #3316: the same operation. Its cause is the ring order: `waterscan.rs:115` sorts the rings core-first, so on an Outside band the first ring of each level is a full slot in the stock. The three rapids may be the jumps between rings that this order makes.
- #3318: the retract plane that the user cannot see. That answer is in this issue.
- #2121 (closed): a clearance plane set inside the stock. Not this case: here the clearance plane is above the stock top.

Done means: a pin test on `fig8.step` with `EM-0800-4FL` and these heights shows no lateral rapid below the clearance plane through stock, with "Hop below clearance" off; the verifier gives no `travels through stock` warning; every shipped golden is byte-identical; an independent Opus read and a hand trace of the three rapids.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> if we look at the lead in and lead out.. the between levels happens at clearance plane.. and between passes happens at retract plane. but i cannot see a retract plane

## What happens

The Lead in / Lead out tab of a 2D Offset operation has two link rows:
- "Between levels" is set to "Clearance plane".
- "Between passes" is set to "Retract plane".

The Heights tab has no Retract Z row. Its Levels group has only "Hop below clearance" (off) and "Stepdown". The viewport labels three planes: Clearance (32.00, stock top +10), Top (22.00) and Bottom (1.50). It labels no retract plane. So the user cannot see or edit the plane that "Between passes" says it uses.

## What the code says

- The hint of the Heights tab says: "the retract plane: on, links hop at Retract Z; off, every link climbs to Clearance Z" (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/heights_page.rs`). The Retract Z row exists only while "Hop below clearance" is on.
- The Lead tab lists "Clearance plane / Retract plane / Keep down" for each link (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/lead_page.rs`). It does not say which height "Retract plane" means when the hop is off.
- The user guide says that a kind that has one gets a retract plane 10 above the stock top (`operations-2d.md`).

## Not known yet

Which height the generator uses for a link set to "Retract plane" when "Hop below clearance" is off, for 2D Offset. The hint of the Heights tab suggests the clearance height. The Lead tab suggests a separate plane. The worker reads the generator and says which one is true.

## Expected

One of these, and the maintainer chooses:
- "Retract plane" is shown on the Heights tab and in the viewport whenever a link uses it, with its value.
- Or the choice is hidden or renamed while no retract plane exists.

The Lead tab then never offers a plane that the user cannot see.

## Related

#3316 is about the same operation (`2D Offset1`, `fig8`, `EM-0800-4FL`). Its warning "rapid move 543 travels through stock (below the clearance plane, or at it below the stock top)" asks why three rapids are below the clearance plane. The answer may depend on this link. The worker of #3316 reads this issue.

Done means: a structural UI test shows that the Lead tab and the Heights tab name the same plane, and that the viewport labels it when a link uses it.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> bug; Movement calcualtion; P2; Example 2D offset set with a outside continment, helixes dowwn inside of the calculated "containmen" and works its way from the inside out.. Which ends up being fully engagend slotting movements not following the rules where it should have been starting outside the part and worked itself in. We might need to add a option prob. undder "passes", that stats "Pass starts at <auto, inside, outside>".. where Auto is current behavior for setting it up and the other two forces either or. So we get control over the fact that it should not try to crate slots in the stock

## What happens

A 2D Offset operation has the containment "Outside". The tool helixes down inside the calculated containment. It then cuts the passes from the inside out. The result is fully engaged slotting moves in the stock.

## Expected

An "Outside" containment starts outside the part and works inward. The tool never makes a fully engaged slot in the stock.

## The change that the maintainer suggests

A new option on the Passes tab: "Pass starts at", with the values Auto, Inside and Outside.
- Auto keeps the current behaviour.
- Inside and Outside force the order.

The user then controls the order and stops the slots. This follows the rule that a strategy fork is an operation parameter with a default.

## Evidence

- Build v0.25.0, commit 7e2a8119 (built 2026-11-22 02:53 UTC). The maintainer sent a screenshot. It is not attached here.
- Operation `2D Offset1`: tool `EM-0800-4FL` (Ø8 end mill), model `fig8`, setup `Setup1`, machine VMC 3-AXIS, post Siemens 840D.
- The status line reads `OK - 8318 moves - 1 warning`. The warning reads: "feed moves 686 and 836 cross in XY at shared depth - repeated on 4 more moves (to 7496)". The operation tree shows 5 warnings.
- Lead in / Lead out tab: Entry type Helix, Helix radius 1.6 mm, Level to level "Same as entry", Between levels "Clearance plane", Between passes "Retract plane".
- The simulation at 60.7 / 1392.8 s shows the tool deep inside the machined area. The cut area around it is a closed slot.
- The maintainer's project file is a local file. Use the tracked model `testdata/models/fig8.step` and the tool `EM-0800-4FL` to reproduce.

## Possible link (not checked)

#2849, test 3 (`shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`) uses the same model, the same tool and an "Outside" containment. Its body says that the last feed ends 31.406 mm from the part outline, and the PR #3267 says that a ring order change fixes it but turns `corner_arc_radius::the_crossing_law_keeps_the_arc_turns_and_crosses_nowhere` red. The two pins want opposite ring orders. A parameter for the order may settle both. The worker checks if this is the same defect and says so on both issues.

## Safety

A fully engaged slot overloads the tool. The toolpath is not a silent wrong cut, but it is a toolpath that the user must not run. If the fix changes pass order or the posted moves, it is under the safety floor: the pin goes red first, and the review is an independent Opus read with a hand trace.

Done means: a pin test shows an Outside containment that starts outside and cuts inward on `fig8.step` with `EM-0800-4FL`, with no move whose engagement is a full slot; the new option and its three values are in the property panel and in MCP; Auto keeps the current output of all shipped goldens.

All three operations generate. `cam.verify()` passes. `cam.post()` refuses the program:

post blocked - 1 warning(s): a feed that turns A from an angle the post does not know - the stated A rate cannot be held

`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs:173-215` leaves the opening rapid moves without a pose.

`crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs:95-108` correctly refuses a feed from an unknown angle when the machine states a rotary rate.

The generator and the post disagree about the initial rotary state.
This report does not ask to remove the rate guard.

body:
## What happens

The OBJ importer refuses a legal face after duplicate vertex records.
I found this while building the five-axis example for #2870.

This OBJ has six vertex records. The second face refers to records 4, 5, and 6.

```obj
v -24 12 0
v -24 11 4
v -16 11 4
f 1 2 3
v -24 12 0
v -16 11 4
v -16 12 0
f 4 5 6
```

The importer reports `vertex reference '5' out of range`.
It must preserve the original vertex indices when it resolves each face.

## Cause

On upstream/main d911f455, `crates/app/src/geometry/import/obj.rs` removes duplicate vertex records before it resolves face indices.
The face handler uses the shortened vertex list.

## Workaround

Write each vertex once. Use its index in that unique list.
The generator for #2870 uses this workaround.

## Done means

The importer accepts the example and preserves both triangles.
Tests cover positive and negative indices after duplicate vertex records.
Malformed references still give a clear error.

effort:high - The fix changes imported geometry. The safety floor applies.

Found while working #2870. Catalog umbrella: #2392.

title: 3+2 under-table refusal gives heights in the tilted frame, not the value that the user typed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

The refusal `FirstTraverseUnderTable` (#3081) gives two heights in the local frame of the 3+2 plane. The message calls them Z values. The user sets the clearance height in the user frame, so the numbers in the message are not values that the user can type.

Generate shifts each height by `h - origin.z` into the tilted frame (`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs`, `judge`). `table_read` returns `limit` as "a local height" (its doc comment), and `judge` puts `start_h` (also local) into `height_mm`. Nothing adds `origin.z` back before the message.

Example from `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_table.rs`, `a_head_tilt_past_90_under_the_table_is_refused_with_lower`:

- The tilt origin is at Z 20 (`ORIGIN_Z`). The user sets the clearance height to 170 (`ORIGIN_Z + 150.0`). The head tilts to B 120.
- The message says: "to the clearance plane at Z150.000 it can go under the table top - lower the clearance plane to Z113.590 or under it".
- In the user frame, the plane is at 170 and the limit is 133.590.

The verdict is correct and the post stays blocked. Only the numbers and the word "Z" in the text are wrong:

- With `origin.z` > 0, a user who types the given limit gets a plane that is lower than necessary.
- With `origin.z` < 0, a user who types the given limit gets the refusal again.
- The heights are measured along the tilted tool axis, not along machine Z, so "Z" is not correct for a tilted plane.

## Related

- #2991 fixes the same defect for `FirstTraverseLow` (PR #3080). That PR adds `in_user_frame` in `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` and a `tilted` text that names the raise without a Z value.
- Found when main was merged into PR #3080. Main added `FirstTraverseUnderTable` after the review of that PR.

## Possible fix

After #3080 merges: extend `in_user_frame` to `FirstTraverseUnderTable` (add `origin.z` to `height_mm` and `limit_mm`). Change the text so that it does not call a height along the tilted axis a Z value, as #2991 does for `FirstTraverseLow`. A cache field can need `#[serde(default)]`, as `tilted` has in #3080.

## Done means

- The under-table refusal on a 3+2 plane gives the plane and the limit in the frame where the user sets the clearance height.
- The text does not call a height along a tilted tool axis a Z value.
- A test pins the two numbers in the user frame (for the case above: 170 and 133.590), and the post stays blocked.

Proposed labels (a contributor cannot set labels): `bug`, `P3`, `effort:medium`, `area:multiaxis`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`. These are the labels of #2991. The defect is a misleading refusal message with a workaround, so `P3`.

Pick the edges.

- A loop that has a drafted side and no modelled chamfer cuts as before, or

The work decides between the two and records the decision.

body:
Reported by flamingfire (Discord, relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), v0.24.0 (f2d78f31), Windows.

## What happens

Project `Rotor.camproj`: model `WVF350-101-453`, a long helical rotor (screw-compressor style lobes, shaft ends) laid along X; machine Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table (A about X), Fanuc post; one 6 mm ball nose; a box stock around the part. Rotary Parallel1 (Source: Stock) and Rotary Contour1 both refuse:

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Rotary Parallel1: invalid machining parameters: the model's normals share no rotation axis - a turned workpiece is rotary work; finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds
```

The refusal is correct for today's design (the rotary operations fit the axis of revolution from the mesh normals, and a helicoid has no common axis). But this part is classic **4-axis wrap work**: it is clamped in the A axis on its own centreline, A turns and the tool follows the lobes. The user has a 4-axis machine, not a 5-axis one, so the message's advice ("finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds") does not help.

## Wanted

1. When the model is not a solid of revolution, the rotary operations can take the axis from the setup instead: the mounted machine's rotary line (A about X) through the WCS / a stated centre (e.g. the stock's or the shaft ends' fitted axis), stated by the user, not guessed.
2. Rotary Parallel (and Rotary Offset roughing) then wrap the toolpath round that axis with the existing radial field check (gouge against the fitted skin = the model itself, stock, part), so a helical rotor, auger, fluted shaft or cam with non-turned features can be finished on 4 axes.
3. Until then, the refusal message names the 4-axis case: e.g. "the model is not a shape of revolution; rotary operations need one today (#this). A part clamped on A that is not turned (helical lobes) is not supported yet" - not only the 5-axis pointer.

## Notes

- The shaft ends of this model are turned; only the lobes are helical. The ends alone would fit an axis, so "fit the axis from the turned faces only" could be a first step.
- Safety floor: the axis must be stated or fitted from real turned faces; a guessed axis that is off by a fraction of a mm wraps a gouge. Refuse when the stated axis and the turned faces disagree.
- Clean-room: published 4-axis wrapping literature only.

Done means: the reporter's kind of part (helical lobes between turned ends, on A about X) generates a Rotary Parallel finish that passes the radial gouge check and posts on the Doosan/Fanuc posts; a part with no turned faces and no stated axis is still refused, with a message that names the 4-axis case.

body:
Requested by @vilts (relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), after the #2603 kit ran clean in his Robodrill's Manual Guide i graphic simulation: today the simulation draws a default blank, and he does not know how to set it by hand.

## What

Manual Guide i reads a blank (stock) definition block near the top of a program and uses it in the animation. An **opt-in** Fanuc post option writes the setup's stock as that block, after the program number and before the first motion.

Codes as the user's reading of the manual summarises them (to be verified against the manual):

| Code | Blank |
|---|---|
| G1902 | rectangular block: B width (X), D depth (Y), H height (Z), I/J/K = X/Y/Z distance from the block's lowest corner to the work origin |
| G1900 | round bar (along Z) |
| G1906 | round bar along X |
| G1901 / G1907 | hollow round bar (along Z / X) |
| G1903 / G1904 | square bar / hollow square bar |

Example (100 x 60 x 30 block, G54 at the top centre): `G1902 B100. D60. H30. I50. J30. K30.`

Source (public Fanuc documentation, behaviour only): Manual Guide i milling and turning operator's manual, https://www.cnc.uk.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/Manual-Guide-Milling-and-Turning-Manual.pdf

## Rules

- **Off by default.** A control without Manual Guide i can alarm on G1902, so the option is per machine (a machine/post property, e.g. "Manual Guide i blank"), never on for every Fanuc output.
- Box stock -> G1902; a cylinder stock -> G1900 (or G1906 when its axis is X); any other stock shape -> no block and a comment saying why, not a wrong block.
- I/J/K come from the setup's WCS origin relative to the stock's minimum corner, in program units (G20/G21), with the signs the manual gives. A yawed or rotated WCS that the block cannot describe -> no block plus a comment.
- No other post output changes (golden files stay the same with the option off).

## Research first (agent)

Read the manual's blank-figure section and confirm: the exact address letters and signs for G1902 and G1900 (incl. the bar's length and the axis position), where in the program the block must stand (before or after G90/G54, before the first tool change), whether it needs Manual Guide i "animation" mode only, and inch behaviour. Record the answers here before code.

## Done means

- The Fanuc post has the option, off by default; with it on, a box stock and a cylinder stock each post the right block (golden tests), and an unsupported stock posts a comment, not a block.
- vilts confirms in his Manual Guide i simulation that the drawn blank matches the stock (one short kit file).
- Clean-room: Fanuc's public manual only; no other CAM's post or output consulted.

body:
Add a clean-room 2-axis wire EDM post (`assets/posts/g-edm.cps`) for G-EDM / `G-RBLv3` controllers.

## Context

`assets/posts/wire-iso.cps` requires `edm.codes.condition` (with `{id}`) and `edm.codes.comp_off`, and it writes `%` tape fences. Public G-EDM documentation (`gedm.org`, `github.com/G-EDM/G-RBL`) states that DIY G-EDM builds control spark power at the controller or firmware instead of via G-code condition words, and `Grbl_Esp32` / Grbl v1.1 rejects bare `%` fences (`error:20`) and `G41`/`G42` radius compensation.

## What this does

- Add `assets/posts/g-edm.cps` (`vendor = "Camcraft"`, `wireEdm = true`, `afterModes = true`, `programUnits = "mm inch"`), with provenance citing public `gedm.org` and `Grbl_Esp32` documentation. Read no `G-RBLv3` source code.
- Register `"G-EDM Wire EDM"` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (`WIRE_POSTS`) and `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` (`BUILTINS` and `embedded()`). Keep `"Generic ISO Wire EDM"` as the default (`WIRE_POSTS[0]`).
- Write `(NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL - CHECK BEFORE CUTTING)` and condition reminders as `(...)` header comments. Do not require `edm.codes`.
- Emit `G21`/`G20`, `G90`, `G17`, `G0`, `G1`, `G2`/`G3` (`I`/`J`), and `M30`, with no `%` fence, no `O`-word, and no `G41`/`G42`.
- Refuse non-`wire_edm` machines, rotaries, `Z` changes, `WireTaper != 0`, `WireFourAxis`, `WireU`/`WireV`, `WireAngle`, `onRadiusCompensation`, `skims`, `onCycle`, `onToolChange`, `SpindleSpeed > 0`, and `AfterOperation === "home"` by name.
- Check `#2697` before coding for any new `G-RBLv3` answers from the reporter (for example whether `G1` requires a dummy `F` word to avoid Grbl `error:22`, `G40`, `M00` threading pauses, or a return move to origin).
- Add golden and refusal tests (`crates/app/tests/g_edm_post.rs`, `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/g-edm/`, `crates/post/tests/script_g_edm.rs`, `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/g-edm/`), and update `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` (`WIRE_POSTS` and `EXTENSIONS`).

## Done means:

- `"G-EDM Wire EDM"` posts a 2-axis `WireContour` golden without `edm.codes` through `posting::post_script`.
- Non-`wire_edm` machines, `G41`/`G42`, taper, 4-axis, skims, and mill goldens refuse by name.
- `cargo xtask gate test g_edm --crate camcraft-app`, `cargo xtask gate test conformance --crate camcraft-app`, and `cargo xtask gate test script_g_edm --crate camcraft-post` pass.

## Why
Only `camcraft-ui` links wgpu today, through the `egui_wgpu::wgpu` re-export (`Cargo.toml` lines 46-47). The generators run in `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-motion`, and in the CLI and MCP with no window. They have no GPU access. The headless device policy exists, but in `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs`.

## What
- A new crate (recommended name `camcraft-gpu`) for headless compute. It holds:
  - The device policy of `headless_gpu.rs` (software adapter first in tests, then hardware), moved down from `camcraft-ui`. `camcraft-ui` then uses it.
  - A capability probe: `DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS`, `max_storage_buffer_binding_size`, `max_compute_workgroup_storage_size`. WebGL2 and GL below ES 3.1 have no compute: the probe says "no compute" by name.
  - One device for each process, made on the first request and cached (`OnceLock`). Never made for each operation or each frame.
  - A switch to turn the GPU off (recommended: `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`) for tests and for machines with bad drivers (#2424, #74).
  - One kernel: conservative facet binning. Input: facet boxes in tile-relative f32, padded by `r` plus a margin. Output: the cell lists.
- The CPU path runs, with the same result, when there is no adapter, the probe fails, the device is lost, or a buffer is past the limit. The log names the reason one time. Never a panic, never `unwrap` on a GPU future.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- Superset parity: for the same facets, each facet in the CPU grid cell of #2619 is in the GPU cell list. Extra GPU entries are permitted.
- Refusals: a buffer past the limit, and a forced "no compute" probe, give `Err` with the reason. The caller uses the CPU grid.
- Adapter policy: the `headless_gpu` rule (#615). No adapter prints a loud SKIP. `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` turns the skip into a failure. The self-hosted runners have the Mesa software drivers (`runners` skill), so the lane runs on lavapipe there.

- A `docs/decisions/` entry is necessary: new crate edges (`camcraft-ui` and `camcraft-app` onto the new crate). The entry lists the imported items and what rebuilds.
- A direct `wgpu` dependency is new for the workspace. The version must be the one that the egui set pins (`=30.0.1` with egui-wgpu `=0.36.2`), so no second wgpu enters the lock. The review sets `needs-maintainer` for this dependency, by AGENTS.md.
- The wgpu version then moves with the egui set (#658, #1118). The decision entry says so.
- `camcraft-motion` gets no GPU dependency. The app computes the GPU result and passes it into motion as a value.

Effort: `effort:high` (several crates, new behaviour with its tests). No posted output changes in this slice.

Done means: the new crate exists with the probe, the cached device, the CPU fallback and the binning kernel; the superset parity test passes on the software adapter; `camcraft-ui` uses the moved device policy; the decision entry is in the PR.

body:
## What happens

`add_tool` gives each new tool the lowest unused number from 1 (camcraft-mcp skill: "Assigns the lowest unused tool number in 1-99999"). Many machines keep a fixed pocket for the probe or a tool setter:

- Tormach PathPilot machines: the probe is **T99** by convention.
- A Hurco VMX30U (WinMax): the export on #2566 has `PROBE` as **T1**.
- A FANUC Robodrill (31i-A5): the owner's **T1** is the probe.

On the last two, CamCraft's first cutting tool becomes T1, so a posted program calls the probe for a face or drill operation. Found while making the Robodrill test kit (#2603): its first version faced with T01, and the owner answered "I will not face with my probe!". The kit was renumbered to T12-T15 by hand.

## Expected

- A machine file can name reserved tool numbers, for example `"tooling": { "reserved": [ { "number": 1, "use": "probe" } ] }` (the exact key to be decided).
- `add_tool` and the tool library skip those numbers for cutting tools; a probe tool takes the probe's number.
- `set_tool_number` to a reserved number for a tool of the wrong kind is refused by name (or warned), and verify/post warn when a program calls a reserved pocket for cutting.
- The Tormach machine files reserve T99 (probe); a generic VMC reserves nothing.

## Done means

A test with a machine file that reserves T1 for the probe: the first added end mill gets T2, the probe gets T1, and a program that cuts with T1 is refused by name.

body:
Part of #1490.

The rest generator currently trusts an entered previous tool. It assumes that tool cut the pocket to the requested depth.

Add a previous-operations mode that derives remaining material from the stock those operations actually leave.

Design decision:
- Keep the entered-tool mode explicit. Add a separate previous-operations mode through an undoable command, the project file, and MCP.
- Read only earlier operations in the same setup, in their actual order. Reuse the established carried-stock infrastructure.
- Require current operation paths and compatible setup coordinates. Refuse missing, stale, or unsupported stock by name, or mark the result incomplete.
- Read remaining stock at every requested cut depth. A shallow roughing pass does not prove that the lower floor is clear.
- Include tool shape, wall and floor allowances, and the supported simulation resolution. Unknown cells remain occupied.
- Pass a conservative remaining-material region to the motion generator. Do not infer cleared volume from the previous tool diameter alone.
- Invalidate the result when an earlier operation changes, moves, is suppressed, or changes its tool or depth.
- Keep the current stock backend. Do not combine this feature with the field-engine migration in #586 or #637.

Tests:
- Compare the rest region with independently simulated earlier operations.
- Test mixed previous tool sizes, bull-nose tools, partial depths, wall allowances, islands, and disconnected cuts.
- Test missing paths, stale paths, operation reordering, changed tools, and unsupported stock frames.
- Prove the plan never removes material from its rest estimate unless the earlier cuts prove that material absent.
- Prove command undo, project save and reopen, MCP editing, and dependency invalidation.
- Remove each depth and stock-validity guard separately. Each mutation must fail its pinning test.

Done means: previous-operations mode uses conservative stock at each depth, passes these tests, and never guesses when stock cannot be established.

Related: #586 and #637 migrate the stock representation. This issue consumes the current representation for 2D rest machining.

Literature: M. Held, On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining, LNCS 500 (1991), https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-54103-9. Z. Yao, S. K. Gupta and D. S. Nau, Algorithms for selecting cutters in multi-part milling problems, Computer-Aided Design 35 (2003), https://www.cs.umd.edu/~nau/papers/yao2003algorithms.pdf.

These sources describe pocket geometry and cutter coverage. The per-depth stock and invalidation contract above is this project's decision. Do not copy another CAM product's code or output.

body:
Add a built-in 3-axis router post for the **RichAuto DSP A11** controller in `assets/posts/richauto.cps`. Register it in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and pin it in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`.

## Context

Issue #1907 confirmed that mkinney's friend runs a **RichAuto DSP A11** handheld controller. Common Laguna Swift (`4x4`, `4x8`, `5x10`) and Grizzly CNC routers (`G0894`, `G0931`, `G0895`) also use this controller.

CamCraft's existing posts (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, `fanuc.cps`, `carvera.cps`, `tinyg.cps`) do not run safely on a RichAuto A11:
- `grblhal.cps` emits `G91.1`, `G94`, `G53 G0 Z...`, `T<n> M6`, and canned cycles. RichAuto A11 uses the pendant `AbsCntr` menu switch (`Off` = incremental) instead of `G91.1`, and basic router firmware can reject canned cycles or `G91.1`.
- `fanuc.cps` emits `%`, `O0001`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, `G49`, `G91 G28 Z0`, and `G84` tapping.

## Specification (OEM manuals only)

1. **Units and file format:** default to `mm` (`G21`) to match RichAuto's internal metric math and avoid `G20` scale errors. Write `.nc` ASCII files with parentheses comments `(...)`. Omit `%`, `O` program numbers, and `;` comments.
2. **Preamble and arcs:** write `G21`, `G90`, `G17`, `G40`, and `G80`. Omit `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, and `G49`. Emit incremental `I`/`J`/`K` matching `AbsCntr = Off`. Handle `G54` cleanly (`G54` default or document `Read G54` vs `Ign G54` in post notes; handle or refuse multi-WCS safely).
3. **Spindle and warm-up:** write `S<rpm> M3`. Add a configurable spindle dwell property (`G04 P<ms>`, default `0`) so the post works alongside the pendant `Spindle Delay` setting. Document 8-step `S1`-`S8` VFD wiring in post comments.
4. **Drilling and tool changes:** expand all canned drill cycles (`G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G73`, `G86`, `G89`) to plain `G0`/`G1` moves (using the pattern in `assets/posts/carvera.cps` and `tinyg.cps`). Refuse mid-program tool changes on the initial 3-axis manual slice (or lift Z cleanly and write `M0` with `(CHANGE TOOL T<n>)` rather than bare `T<n> M6`).
5. **Refusals and footer:** refuse `G84` tapping, `G41`/`G42` cutter compensation, and probing. Retract Z to clearance height in work coordinates, stop spindle (`M5`) and coolant (`M9` if active), and end with `M30` (no trailing `%`).

## Rules

- Clean room: use only RichAuto DSP A11 OEM documentation, RS-274 / ISO 6983 standards, and CamCraft repository patterns (`assets/posts/AGENTS.md`). Do not read or copy Autodesk, HSMWorks, or third-party CAM posts.

## Done means

- `assets/posts/richauto.cps` exists and registers in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`.
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` passes for `RichAuto DSP A11` across all mill goldens and refuses `G84`, `G41`/`G42`, and probing by name.
- Posted `.nc` output uses `G21`, incremental `I`/`J`, expanded drilling moves, `(...)` comments, safe Z retract, and `M30` with no `%`, `O` headers, `G91.1`, `G43`, or `G49`.
- Decision entry added under `docs/decisions/`.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "we should be able to set start points on generated path and also exit points.. So the path gets regenerated to those."

What is missing: where an operation starts cutting and where it leaves is chosen by the generator alone. The user cannot say "enter here" or "leave here", for example to keep the entry mark off a visible face, to start a contour away from a clamp, or to end next to the following feature.

Wanted: on the operations where it has a meaning (2D Contour, Pocket, Adaptive, Face, Slot, Bore, and the 3D finishing passes that have a free start), two optional picks:
- Start point(s): picked in the viewport (a point on the model, a sketch point or typed coordinates). For a closed contour the path is re-sequenced to begin at the pick's nearest point on the chain, with its lead-in there; for a pocket or adaptive region the entry (helix, ramp or plunge) is placed at the pick. One pick per chain or region; chains with no pick keep the automatic choice.
- Exit point(s): the same for where the pass ends and the lead-out is placed.

Changing a pick is an undoable command (it edits the operation parameters) and regenerates the path. MCP: the same parameters on the operation tools.

Safety: a pick is a wish, never an override of a check. If the entry, lead or ramp at the picked place does not fit (helix does not fit in the region, lead-in gouges a wall, the point is outside the machinable region or inside a keep-out or fixture), the operation is refused by name or marked incomplete, saying which pick and why; it never moves the entry silently and never posts a path that the collision or gouge checks would refuse at the automatic entry.

Related: the companion issue on pre-drilled holes as entry positions (filed with this one).

Done means: a closed 2D contour with a picked start begins and leads in at that point and, with a picked exit, leads out there (golden CL); a pocket enters at its picked point; an impossible pick is refused by name in a test; undo and redo restore the previous path; the MCP tools take the picks; the structural UI test covers the two pick rows.

body:
The chamfer/taper kind is a sharp cone only: no tip diameter, no tip radius, and no tapered flank above a non-sharp tip.

**Where:** `Taper` is "a cone widening upward from its virtual sharp tip" (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs`, Taper doc; `is_sane` near `:305`).

**Effect:**
- Flat-tip chamfer mills, V-engravers with a point radius, countersinks and combined center drills (both with a real tip diameter), and tapered end mills with a ball or flat tip can't be described.
- Writing them as sharp cones misstates where the cutter actually is: the depth for a given chamfer width is wrong by the tip.

**Fix sketch:** `Taper` gains an optional tip diameter and tip radius (and a tip form: flat or ball). The chamfer-depth math, the sim and the gouge laws use the real tip.

Effort: max (geometry).

**Done means:** a flat-tip chamfer and a radiused-point V-bit chamfer to the right width at the right depth; pinned.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
